papers.title: DART-SD: Diamond-topology Aware Retrieval and Tuning for Self-Distillation of Multi-Turn Tool-Calling Agents
papers.abstract_en: Equipping Large Language Models (LLMs) with multi-turn tool-calling capabilities is essential for building autonomous agents. However, progress is fundamentally limited by the reliance on full-length trajectory imitation. For tasks involving multiple order-independent sub-goals, the optimal solution space forms a vast combinatorial diamond lattice. Forcing this rich topology into monolithic trajectories causes a severe topological collapse, indiscriminately penalizing valid alternative explorations and severely degrading policy diversity. To address this, we propose DART-SD (Diamond-topology Aware Retrieval and Tuning for Self-Distillation), a novel framework that shifts the paradigm from global forcing to topology-guided localized correction. DART-SD first models the execution process as a converging Interaction-State Transition Graph (ISTG), faithfully capturing the inherent diamond topology of successful and failed exploratory paths. During autonomous rollouts, the framework identifies the Critical Topological Breakpoint (CTB) and retrieves success-supported recovery references. Finally, we introduce a progressive self-distillation paradigm through CTB-guided localized supervision, ensuring that the training loss is calculated exclusively on the generated recovery steps while strictly protecting the valid reasoning prefix from destructive gradient updates. Experiments on complex multi-turn tool-calling benchmarks demonstrate that DART-SD significantly outperforms traditional full-trajectory baselines.

summary_es.tldr: DART-SD mejora agentes LLM para llamar herramientas, superando la limitación de imitar trayectorias completas.
summary_es.problema: Los agentes LLM que usan herramientas en múltiples turnos sufren una degradación severa de la diversidad de políticas al forzar la imitación de trayectorias completas, especialmente en tareas con sub-objetivos independientes.
summary_es.propuesta: DART-SD propone un marco que modela el proceso de ejecución como un grafo de transición de estados (ISTG) que respeta la topología de diamante. Identifica puntos críticos de ruptura (CTB) y recupera referencias de éxito para guiar una auto-destilación localizada, corrigiendo solo los pasos de recuperación sin alterar el razonamiento previo válido.
summary_es.resultados: DART-SD supera significativamente a los métodos tradicionales de trayectoria completa en benchmarks complejos de llamadas a herramientas multi-turno.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Permite crear agentes de IA más robustos y diversos, capaces de manejar tareas complejas con múltiples pasos de forma más eficiente y menos propensa a errores.

papers.title: ContextPilot: Teaching Agents for Proactive Context Management via Fine-grained RL
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon agentic tasks require large language models (LLMs) to iteratively retrieve, integrate, and maintain dispersed information across multi-turn interactions, but preserving all interaction histories leads to a continuously growing working context. Recent proactive context management methods allow models to edit their own working context with specialized tools, yet they still face three key limitations: (1) a limited toolset restricted to search, deletion, and summarization, with no support for global planning, long-term memory, and adaptive compression; (2) inefficient exploration that treats context management actions uniformly despite their heterogeneous impacts on final outcomes; and (3) coarse-grained credit assignment that assigns the final trajectory-level reward to all intermediate context editing actions during RL. To bridge these gaps, we introduce ContextPilot, a proactive context management framework for long-horizon agentic reasoning. Our approach systematically augments the toolset with planning, long-term memory, and soft context offloading tools. We further propose an RL method tailored for context management, which uses context and entropy variation to identify critical editing decisions for branch sampling and estimates action-level advantages from all branched trajectories that pass through the corresponding context editing action. Experiments on long-context QA and deep search tasks show that ContextPilot achieves stronger performance with a more compact working context, consistently outperforming existing baselines across various base models and benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/Tencent/ContextPilot.

summary_es.tldr: ContextPilot revoluciona la gestión del contexto en IA, permitiendo a los agentes planificar y recordar proactivamente para tareas complejas.
summary_es.problema: Las tareas de IA a largo plazo se ven obstaculizadas por la gestión ineficiente del contexto, que crece continuamente y limita las capacidades de planificación, memoria y compresión adaptativa de los modelos.
summary_es.propuesta: ContextPilot introduce un marco de gestión proactiva del contexto que amplía el conjunto de herramientas con capacidades de planificación, memoria a largo plazo y descarga de contexto adaptable, junto con un método de aprendizaje por refuerzo (RL) optimizado para la toma de decisiones críticas en la edición del contexto.
summary_es.resultados: ContextPilot logra un rendimiento superior con un contexto de trabajo más compacto, superando consistentemente a los métodos existentes en tareas de QA de contexto largo y búsqueda profunda.
summary_es.por_que_importa: Mejora significativamente la eficiencia y eficacia de los modelos de IA en tareas complejas y de larga duración, reduciendo la carga computacional y mejorando la precisión al gestionar de forma inteligente la información.
